Title: Maldives, Malaysia strengthen defence and Islamic cooperation
Article:
MALÉ: Maldives and Malaysia have strengthened their institutional ties through new cooperation agreements in defence and Islamic affairs, while reaffirming their shared positions on Palestine and climate change.
Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu said the agreements witnessed during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's state visit would open new avenues for practical cooperation between the two countries.
"Today, we also witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith," he said.
"These agreements open new avenues for practical cooperation and further strengthen the institutional foundations of our bilateral relationship."
On international issues, Muizzu said Maldives and Malaysia remained united by shared Islamic values and a common commitment to justice, peace and human dignity.
He said the two countries had reiterated their "unequivocal and steadfast solidarity" with the Palestinian people and their right to self-determination and an independent and sovereign state based on pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Muizzu also welcomed closer Maldives engagement with Aseam and congratulated Malaysia on its successful chairmanship of the regional grouping in 2025.
On climate change, he said Maldives and Malaysia had reaffirmed the urgency of addressing the threat ahead of COP31 in Türkiye in November.
"For the Maldives and other small island developing states, climate change is not a distant challenge; it is an immediate reality," he said.
Muizzu called for predictable, accessible and adequate climate adaptation financing while maintaining efforts to keep the rise in global temperatures below the critical 1.5-degree threshold.
He described Anwar's visit as a reaffirmation of the "deep fraternal bonds, mutual respect, and trust" between the two countries.
"The Maldives and Malaysia are not only close friends; we are brothers, bound by shared values, shared aspirations, and a shared commitment to a better future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia to open trading at planned commodity bourse on January 4, official says
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia plans to start trading at its new commodity exchange on Jan 4, 2027, with tin and ferronickel to be included in the opening transactions, the chief supervisor of the commodity exchange said on Tuesday.
State miners are expected to be among the first participants in the exchange, according to a slide presented at a parliamentary hearing by chief supervisor Sarjito, who goes by a single name.
The commodity exchange, to be known as ICOMEX, is part of President Subianto's push to expand state control over the country's vast natural resources and their proceeds.
In a fiery speech last month, Prabowo said Indonesia would rather keep its resources than sell them too cheaply.
Friderica Widyasari Dewi, chairperson of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), said the exchange would help combat under-invoicing and end transfer-pricing practices for commodity exports.
The OJK expects to issue regulations for the exchange on Sept 17 and the bourse will be created on the same day. The license for the bourse will be issued on Jan 1.
"Trading on the mineral and strategic commodity exchange is expected to launch in early January, January 4, 2027, through the ICOMEX entity," Sarjito said, referring to the name of the planned exchange.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia raises October crude palm oil reference price, duty remains at 10pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has raised its October crude palm oil reference price to a level that maintains the export duty at 10 per cent, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Tuesday.
The world's second-largest palm exporter calculated a reference price of 4,452.66 ringgit (US$1,091.34) per tonne for October.
The September reference price was 4,392.32 ringgit a tonne, and incurred a duty of 10 per cent.
The export tax structure starts at three per cent for crude palm oil in a 2,250-to-2,400 ringgit-per-tonne range. The maximum tax rate is set at 10 per cent when prices exceed 4,050 ringgit a tonne.

Title: YTL Power, Ganda Power secure four additional Siemens Energy gas turbine units
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd, Ganda Power and Siemens Energy have signed reservation agreements for four additional SGT-9000HL gas turbine units.
In a statement issued by YTL Power, the company said the latest reservations bring the total number of units secured by Ganda and YTL Power to seven, including three units obtained earlier.
The turbines are intended to support power generation projects in Malaysia and the wider region with a combined capacity of over 5,250 megawatts (MW).
"Siemens Energy has been a trusted partner for more than three decades, with a shared commitment to engineering excellence and long-term investment.
"Together with Ganda, these additional turbines bring our total arrangements to seven units and strengthen our ability to pursue reliable, efficient and competitive energy solutions globally," said its managing director Datuk Seri Yeoh Seok Hong.
He said energy is the foundation of the artificial intelligence (AI) economy, hence, by combining power generation experience and expanding capabilities in data centres and AI, the group is building the infrastructure that would support its customers' growth and the industries of the future.
According to YTL Power, Siemens Energy's SGT-9000HL gas turbine family is designed to deliver high efficiency, operational flexibility and reliability, supporting dependable electricity supply as power systems integrate more renewable energy.

Title: Malaysia to resolve bureaucratic hurdles affecting Maldivian students, healthcare
Article:
MALÉ: Malaysia will seek to resolve bureaucratic issues affecting Maldivian students and their parents, while strengthening cooperation in healthcare, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said more than 2,000 Maldivian students were currently studying in Malaysia, reflecting the confidence placed by Maldives in the country's education system.
"We need to reciprocate the facility," he said, referring to Malaysia's efforts to ensure a conducive environment for Maldivian students.
Anwar said he had discussed with his Cabinet colleagues some "teething bureaucratic issues" involving parents accompanying their children and would seek to resolve them at the next Cabinet meeting.
"I don't think it is the issue of policy differences. We don't have problems with Maldivians living in Malaysia, working in Malaysia, or even studying in Malaysia.
"So I think we will showcase this and respond positively," he said in a joint press conference with Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu here.
On healthcare, Anwar said Malaysia's Madani economic framework placed strong emphasis on compassion, care and support, including mental health and persons with disabilities.
"I don't believe that this issue cannot be resolved because it's part of our national philosophy," he said, adding that Malaysia wanted the matter resolved immediately.
Anwar said the number of cases involved was relatively small and should not prevent the two countries from finding practical solutions.
Meanwhile, Muizzu highlighted the importance of Malaysia's long-standing role in developing Maldivian human capital.
He expressed appreciation for Malaysia's continued support through the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme and for expanding higher education scholarship opportunities for Maldivian students.
"We agreed to work towards greater visa facilitation, expanded scholarship opportunities, and joint research initiatives," he said.
He said the two countries would also strengthen institutional partnerships between their higher education institutions.
Muizzu also thanked Malaysia for the care and hospitality extended to the Maldivian community in the country, saying the two sides had discussed practical measures to address challenges faced by Maldivian students and patients seeking specialised healthcare in Malaysia.
Tourism, he said, remained an important bridge between the two countries.
"We agreed to deepen cooperation in tourism promotion, the halal industry, cultural exchanges, and Muslim-friendly travel," he said.
"We will also work together to increase tourism flows between our two countries and promote sustainable ecotourism, creating great opportunities for people-to-people connections and mutually beneficial economic activity in trade and investment.
"We have explored concrete pathways to further expand economic cooperation. Importantly, we agreed to initiate negotiations for a preferential trade agreement, which has the potential to create new opportunities for businesses in both countries."
Muizzu said Maldives and Malaysia would work to increase tourism flows between the two countries and promote sustainable ecotourism, creating opportunities for stronger people-to-people ties and mutually beneficial economic activity.
The president said Anwar's visit further strengthened the countries' 58-year diplomatic partnership and reciprocated his official visit to Malaysia in April 2025.

Title: Danish PM slams 'reckless action' of Russian frigate firing flares
Article:
COPENHAGEN: A Russian warship has fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter in the Baltic Sea, with the Russian ambassador summoned over the incident, Denmark officials said on Tuesday.
The incident occurred on Monday, the same day that Nato jets shot down a drone over Lithuania, the latest security incident on the alliance's eastern flank during Russia's war with Ukraine.
"One of the air force's Fennec helicopters was today fired at with flares during a routine photographic operation of a Russian frigate, which was located in international waters off Gedser," the armed forces said in a statement late Monday.
The frigate had fired "two flares towards the helicopter. One of the flares passed at close range to the helicopter," it added.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen slammed the incident as "reckless action from Russia."
"Russian actions are meant to intimidate and divide. They will not succeed. We will not waver," Frederiksen said in a statement on X.
Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen meanwhile said the actions were "completely unacceptable and could have put human lives at risk."
"I have therefore summoned the Russian ambassador for a discussion about the incident," he said in a statement sent to AFP.
"Russia is gradually shifting the boundary for what they consider acceptable behaviour," he warned.
"That is something we cannot accept," he said.
Danish media reported that Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus had summoned representatives of the parties in parliament for a briefing on the incident at the defence ministry.
Tensions over the Baltic Sea have risen sharply since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as Go-To-Safety-Point locations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur police have proposed making KK Mart convenience stores Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations as part of a strategic collaboration to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team has identified around 700 KK Mart branches in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor that operate 24 hours, have bright lighting, and are equipped with centralised closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, which have the potential to be safe locations for the public to seek assistance during emergencies.
"We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. At the same time, we will enhance cooperation in terms of patrolling and monitoring so that these premises become safe places for the public," he said at a press conference for the opening of the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur Police headquarters today, which was also attended by KK Supermart & Superstore Sdn Bhd founder and executive chairman Datuk Seri Dr Chai Kee Kan.
Fadil said that they are also looking into the possibility of being granted access to the centralised CCTV of the convenience store chain, which simultaneously strengthens security monitoring in the surrounding area.
According to police, the GTSP programme is an initiative that creates a network of strategic partner premises as safety points for the public to obtain immediate assistance in the event of an emergency, a crime, or a security threat.
Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters is the first convenience store branch in the police building.
Commenting on the control of goods sold at the KK Mart premises in the police headquarters, he said that the business operations are subject to government premises regulations, and any prohibited goods will not be allowed for sale.
Meanwhile, Chai said that there are currently around 1,100 KK Mart branches nationwide, and he sees great potential to place the convenience store in government buildings.
He also welcomed KK Mart's initiative as a GTSP and was willing to share CCTV footage from the convenience store chain to assist police investigations. — BERNAMA

Title: What makes us proud to be Malaysian: Peace, unity and hope
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Peace, unity in diversity and a shared hope for a better future are among the things Malaysians say make them proud of their country as they mark the 63rd Malaysia Day tomorrow.
For Inland Revenue Board officer Intan Shazwani Ahmad Mazlan, 37, a sense of safety and Malaysia's remarkable diversity stand out most.
"I am proud to be a Malaysian because I feel safe in my own homeland.
"Malaysia is also unique because it has various races and communities living together. What I love most is that this diversity makes our food and culture very special," she told the New Straits Times.
[[nid:1533367]]
Her hope for the nation was simple but heartfelt — that peace and harmony would endure, and that Malaysia would continue to be led by great, trustworthy and capable leaders who can steer the country forward.
Retired civil servant Mohd Yunos Mohamad, 79, echoed similar sentiments, pointing to Malaysia's multi-ethnic, multicultural and multi-religious fabric as a source of deep pride.
"I am proud because Malaysia always moves forward as a progressive nation. God willing, Malaysia will continue forward as a prestigious country," he said.
[[nid:1533366]]
Architectural draftsman Miao Yap, 39, offered a more personal reflection.
"I have never been prouder. My wish is that we Malaysians can walk three steps forward but only one step backwards.
"We move forward and grow together," she said.
For recent graduate Noorizzati Jabannoor, 23, Malaysia's pride lies not only in its ethnic mosaic of Malays, Chinese and Indians, but also in the richness of its indigenous communities, including the Orang Asli, Iban and Bidayuh.
Her wish was for a Malaysia that is just, sustainable and inclusive, finding common ground in diversity while preserving harmony.
"Living in a multiracial society in peace, where festivals of all communities are celebrated joyfully together as one family," she said.
Inland Revenue Board officer Nor Hidayah Abdullah, 39, rounded off the sentiments with a hope that captured what many others felt — that the unity and peace the country has built over 63 years will not only endure but grow stronger.
"My hope is for Malaysia to remain peaceful, progressive and prosperous. I hope Malaysians will always be united, respect one another and together build a better future for our country," she said.

Title: Mahmoud Khalil sues Columbia for alleged failure to protect pro-Palestinian students
Article:
NEW YORK: Mahmoud Khalil and other pro-Palestinian student activists sued Columbia University on Monday, accusing the Ivy League school of being deliberately indifferent to years of pervasive harassment because of their advocacy.
Khalil became a face of the Trump administration crackdown on students' pro-Palestinian protests after US immigration agents arrested him in March 2025 in the lobby of his university residence, though he was a lawful permanent resident — or green card holder — and not accused of a crime.
The complaint filed in Manhattan federal court by Khalil, the SIPA Palestine Working Group and its president, Mohammad Zubairi, said Columbia violated federal civil rights law through its failure to protect students from threats, doxxing and other harassment based on their perceived Arab or Muslim ancestry, or their advocacy for Palestinian rights.
The war in Gaza still sparks fierce debate at schools including Columbia, where the central pedestrian walkway across campus has been closed for nearly three years as the university tries to balance safety concerns against the desire for greater normalcy and openness.
At a press conference at Columbia announcing the lawsuit, Khalil said the university exhibited a "rotten, institutionalised anti-Palestinian bigotry" entrenched in every department and backed by its board of trustees.
"We are suing because no student, regardless of their background, should go through the hell that Columbia put us through over all these years," Khalil said.
Columbia declined to comment on the lawsuit, but a spokeswoman said: "Creating a campus environment where every member of our community feels welcome, supported, and safe is fundamental to who we are as a university. It is also a responsibility we take seriously."
Khalil said he began reporting harassment during the spring semester in 2023, several months before Israel went to war in Gaza.
The complaint said that instead of investigating reported harassment, Columbia treated pro-Palestinian protests as "security risks" and revised its policies to treat any on-campus criticism of Israel's military or government conduct as subject to discipline.
"Defendants' failure to respond to Mr. Khalil's, Mr. Zubairi's, and other PWG members' legitimate reports of ongoing harassment and violence, and the retaliatory actions they actively took in response to these reports, placed PWG members at risk of violence and caused sustained, ongoing harm," the complaint said.
The protests at Columbia divided the university, with many supporting the protesters and others saying they felt unsafe or considered some activity antisemitic.
They led to the spread of so-called solidarity encampments on dozens of college campuses, and to the resignation of Columbia's president.
Khalil is an Algerian citizen born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria.
He spent 104 days in a Louisiana jail following his arrest, missing the birth of his first child, before being released on bail.
Khalil still faces possible deportation, after a federal appeals court in Philadelphia said a district court judge lacked jurisdiction when he ordered Khalil's release from custody last year.
SIPA is short for Columbia's School of International and Public Affairs, where Khalil had been a graduate student.
Khalil also sued Columbia in March 2025, less than one week after his arrest, challenging the university's disclosure of student disciplinary records to a House of Representatives committee.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muhyiddin grateful for acquittal, hopes to be freed on remaining charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said he felt vindicated by the High Court's decision to acquit him of four of seven charges linked to the Jana Wibawa programme.
He said he had been confident of his innocence from the outset.
Muhyiddin, who expressed gratitude to God following the decision, said the acquittal brought him a sense of relief after maintaining all along that he was not guilty.
"I thank God for the decision. I thank my lawyers who defended me. I welcome the decision and I am relieved.
"I hope I will be freed on the remaining charges," he said at the courts complex lobby.

Title: Haze: Johan Setia records highest API at 188, 47 stations remain unhealthy  [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in several areas across the country remained at unhealthy levels, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 188 as at 4pm today.
According to the latest data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 177, followed by Nilai in Negeri Sembilan at 176 and Putrajaya at 174.
Shah Alam recorded 173, while Seremban and Tangkak each recorded 172.
IPD Serian in Sarawak recorded 171, followed by Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur at 169.
Klang in Selangor, Pasir Gudang in Johor and Indera Mahkota Kuantan in Pahang each recorded an API reading of 167, while Tanjung Malim in Perak and Petaling Jaya in Selangor recorded 166 each.
Banting in Selangor, Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai in Melaka, and Kota Tinggi in Johor each recorded 164.
Kuala Selangor in Selangor, Temerloh and Jerantut in Pahang recorded 163 each, while Balok Baru Kuantan recorded 162.
Larkin in Johor and Kemaman in Terengganu recorded 161 each, followed by Seri Manjung in Perak, Batu Pahat and Pengerang in Johor at 160 each.
Port Dickson in Negeri Sembilan recorded 159, while Paka in Terengganu recorded 158.
Tasek Ipoh in Perak and Kuala Terengganu recorded 157 each, followed by Balik Pulau in Penang and Rompin in Pahang at 154 each.
Sungai Petani in Kedah and Samarahan in Sarawak recorded 153 each, while Minden in Penang recorded 152.
Seberang Jaya in Penang recorded 139, followed by Segamat in Johor at 117.
Pegoh Ipoh in Perak recorded the lowest API reading among the stations listed, at 104.
Under the API classification used by APIMS, readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.

Title: Indonesia records 1,437 hotspots as transboundary haze persists
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia recorded 1,437 high‑confidence hotspots as of Monday night, with Kalimantan accounting for the bulk of detections as transboundary haze persisted across the region.
Indonesia's Forestry Ministry official Lusiana Martapuri said Central Kalimantan recorded the highest concentration with 689 hotspots, followed by West Kalimantan with 203, South Sumatra 116, South Kalimantan 112 and Jambi nine.
No high‑confidence hotspots were detected in Riau, she said, adding that firefighting efforts are focused mainly on Kalimantan, particularly Central and West Kalimantan.
"In general, air quality conditions in Indonesia remain varied, with most areas in the good to moderate categories, although several areas in Sumatra and Kalimantan are still recording unhealthy to very unhealthy conditions, and hazardous levels in certain areas," she said in a video posted on the ministry's social media on Tuesday.
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre reported moderate transboundary haze over Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore.
In Malaysia, 38 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index readings as of 9 am Tuesday, while Singapore also reported unhealthy air quality across all five regions.
Lusiana said 53 aircraft remain deployed — 34 for water bombing and 19 for aerial patrols — alongside weather modification operations.
The aerial response is reinforced by three CH‑47 Chinook helicopters from Japan for water‑bombing, while ground teams continue firefighting, containment, mopping‑up and cooling operations.– BERNAMA

Title: SMK Ghafar Baba tops DRB-HICOM-Harian Metro Melaka pantun competition
Article:
BANDA HILIR: SMK Ghafar Baba emerged as champion of the 2026 DRB-HICOM-Harian Metro Proverb-themed Pantun Competition at the Melaka state level yesterday.
The victory earned SMK Ghafar Baba a place in the Southern Zone final at Maktab Abu Bakar in Johor Bahru, Johor, on Sept 29, where it will compete for the overall title.
The prize presentation ceremony was officiated by DRB-HICOM Berhad chief communications officer Cairil Irwan Amir.
Also present were Harian Metro Group editor Husain Jahit, Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) Language and Literature Development Department director Abang Haliman Abang Julai, Melaka Education Department director Mahfudzah Mohamed Noor and SMK Tinggi Melaka principal Johan Othman.
SMK Ghafar Baba clinched the title through the performances of four contestants — Putera Hirfan Abdullah, Muhammad Hasif Muhammad Fazlie, Muhammad Hafiy Iskandar Mohd Hazri and Nur Aisyy Humairah Mohd Rajab.
SMK Pernu placed fourth, receiving RM800 in cash, a trophy and a certificate, while the school received RM550.
SMK Ayer Keroh and SMKA Sharifah Rodziah shared fifth place, with each receiving RM600 in cash, a DRB-HICOM trophy and certificate. Their respective schools received RM550 each.
More than 300 students attended the competition, which was judged by four professionals.
They are composer, lyricist and pantun writer Dr Hairul Anuar Harun, national-level DBP judge Dr Faezah Muhayat, Musazliza Mustan Shir and pantun researcher, scholar and author Dr Mohamad Shaidan.
In the final, SMK Ghafar Baba will face the champions from Negri Sembilan and Johor.
Harian Metro Group editor Husain Jahit said the competition reflected the synergy between the media, corporate sector and education in nurturing confident, sharp-minded young people grounded in national identity.
He said Harian Metro's role extended beyond news reporting to preserving the nation's identity and heritage, particularly by bringing the art of pantun closer to younger generations.
"Media plays a critical role as a catalyst and bridge in bringing traditional heritage such as pantun closer to the younger generation.
"We want to prove that pantun is not a relic of the past that is fading with time, but a dynamic, creative form of communication that remains relevant to the spirit of today's youth," he said.
He added that the strong response throughout the qualifying rounds showed that proverb-themed pantun exchanges continued to resonate with young people.
"The participants' ability to master the art of spontaneous pantun exchanges also shows that this heritage continues to serve as a medium for uniting the hearts and minds of young people from diverse backgrounds," he said.
Meanwhile, Cairil said the competition reflected DRB-HICOM's commitment to empowering young people through talent development and lifelong learning opportunities.
He said the competition was not merely about finding a champion, but also served as a platform to revive the art of pantun among students while developing their creativity and communication skills.
"For DRB-HICOM, this competition is not just about who becomes champion. More importantly, it gives students the experience of having the courage to stand before an audience, express their views confidently and communicate clearly.
"These values are important in helping them grow in whatever fields they pursue in the future," he said.
DRB-HICOM is Harian Metro's strategic collaboration partner in organising the competition.
The programme was initiated by DRB-HICOM and introduced in 2025 as a pilot project at the Selangor state level.

Title: From barefoot schoolboy to chief justice: Remembering Eusoff Chin
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: He walked barefoot to school, sold his mother's kuih at a railway station during the Japanese occupation and studied beneath streetlights because there was no proper light at home.
Decades later, Tun Mohd Eusoff Chin rose to become the country's second chief justice.
But to his youngest daughter, Zuliana Eusoff, the man who reached the pinnacle of the judiciary remained simply a gentle father who never allowed the stature of his office to define him.
Speaking at a reference proceeding held in his memory at the Palace of Justice here today, Zuliana recalled her father's journey from a childhood of hardship to the country's highest judicial office.
Eusoff grew up in a large family with little to spare, and he and his brothers often walked barefoot to school in Kampar.
During the Japanese occupation, he sold his mother's kuih at the railway station, sometimes only realising after a train had left that soldiers had taken them without paying.
With no proper light at home, he studied beneath streetlights and excelled in the Senior Cambridge Examination.
He later entered Anderson School in Ipoh but had to leave after only three months following his father's death, as the family could no longer afford his education.
Despite being top of his school, his scholarship application was unsuccessful.
His fortunes began to change after he became a probationary teacher in Kelantan in 1955.
A senior teacher recognised his potential and encouraged him to do more with his life, an intervention Zuliana described as an important turning point.
The following year, Eusoff joined the public service as a Labour Officer before entering the Kelantan Civil Service as an assistant district officer, where he also sat as a lay magistrate.
His ability caught the attention of then Supreme Court registrar Tan Sri S. S. Gill, who introduced him to then Chief Justice Sir James Thompson.
Eusoff eventually secured a scholarship and went to Lincoln's Inn in 1961 before being called to the English Bar in 1963.
After serving in numerous legal and judicial positions, he was elevated to the High Court bench in 1982 and appointed a Supreme Court judge in 1992.
On Sept 25, 1994, the boy who once studied beneath streetlights became the top judge.
At home, however, Zuliana remembered a man of few words whose pleasures were simple: fishing, mamak breakfasts, books and music.
He sang and played the guitar and electric organ, and gave his children the freedom to pursue their own interests.
He also taught them to listen to others, think for themselves and never abandon what they believed to be right simply because another path was easier.
Despite devoting more than four decades to the judiciary and public service, Zuliana said her
father's legacy to the family
went beyond his judicial achievements.
"He never allowed the stature of his office to define him at home. He simply came home as our father."
"As his daughter, I am immensely proud, not simply because he became Chief Justice, but because of the man he remained before, during and after the titles."
Malaysia, then known as Malaya, was under Japanese occupation from 1941 to 1945 during the Second World War.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pesta Pulau Pinang to continue at new venue
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government will continue Pesta Pulau Pinang this year, with Padang Menora being considered as the new venue after the festival lost its long-time site at the Sungai Nibong fairground.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state was considering the venue in collaboration with the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda), which had offered the site.
"The state government has indeed planned to continue Pesta Pulau Pinang from this year, but we can no longer use the Sungai Nibong fairground for the event.
"So, we are considering where to hold it, and we have received cooperation from Perda, which has offered a venue in Padang Menora," he said after officiating the closing ceremony of the Penang2030 national-level public speaking competition 2026 in Batu Uban.
Chow said although the proposed venue was smaller than the Sungai Nibong site, it was deemed suitable for the event and would allow the long-running festival to continue.
He added that the state executive council had decided to retain the name Pesta Pulau Pinang, given its strong recognition among the public after five decades.
Chow said the festival was scheduled to run for a month from Dec 1 to 31.
The 2025/2026 edition was the final Pesta Pulau Pinang to be held at the Sungai Nibong fairground before the site is used for the construction of a depot and station for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project.
It was previously reported that Pesta Pulau Pinang would be suspended for six years to make way for construction of the LRT line.
The annual fair was introduced under the leadership of Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, who served as Penang chief minister from 1969 to 1990.
Launched in 1970, the fair was established to spur business activity and create economic opportunities at a time when the state was grappling with high unemployment and a challenging economic climate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NADA to station officers at RTS Link entry points from Dec 31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) will station officers from its Anti-Drugs Border Unit (UAS) at the two entry points of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link ahead of its operation on Dec 31.
NADA director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the officers would be stationed at the Bukit Chagar Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex in Johor and the Woodlands North Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex in Singapore.
He said the matter was among those discussed during a bilateral meeting between NADA and Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) in the capital today.
"The opening of the RTS Link service is set to significantly increase cross-border movement, thereby requiring strong coordination and preparedness among the enforcement agencies of both countries to ensure a safe environment free from the threat of drugs.
"This discussion provided an important platform for NADA and CNB to detail operational arrangements, mechanisms for coordinating officers, as well as rapid communication channels at the main entry points, namely ICQS Bukit Chagar in Johor and CIQ Woodlands North in Singapore," he said in a statement.
Ruslin said the meeting, which he co-chaired with CNB deputy director (Operations) Aaron Tang, aimed to strengthen strategic and operational cooperation, particularly in addressing border security challenges ahead of the RTS Link's launch.
The two agencies also reviewed emerging cross-border drug threats, including the use of technology and online platforms, new psychoactive substances (NPS) and the latest drug-smuggling modus operandi.
He said the success of bilateral cooperation depended not only on official discussions, but also on concrete and practical follow-up actions by the operational teams on both sides.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC officer withdraws police report against Muhyiddin's lawyer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer has withdrawn a police report against Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's lawyer over an issue raised during the Bersatu president's Jana Wibawa trial.
MACC investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini said his assistant withdrew the report at 12.45pm today.
The report was lodged for police to investigate how businessman Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad's statement recording in a separate case came into the defence team's possession, despite the document allegedly being unrelated to Muhyiddin.
Mazery, who is the 29th prosecution witness said, checks at the MACC headquarters found no information had been leaked by the agency's officers involving the recording or documents in question.
"I am satisfied that there was no evidence or any documents that came from MACC officers themselves.
"Therefore, I immediately instructed my assistant to withdraw the report at 12.45pm today," he said.
Mazery said this during Muhyiddin's Jana Wibawa trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin. Muhyiddin is facing three charges of abuse of power in the case.
He said the MACC had also requested that his assistant's statement be recorded by the police to enable a no further action (NFA) decision to be issued on the police report.
"With this, I hope Amer Hamzah can understand and accept the swift action I have taken in the interest of today's proceedings and their harmony," he said.
During this morning's proceedings, Amer Hamzah had applied for Mazery to be held in
contempt of court.
Amer Hamzah said Mazery's action in lodging a police report over a document submitted by the defence could be considered contempt of court as he has previously been ordered by the court not to communicate with any party while still giving evidence.
Amer Hamzah said the police report was subsequently reported by the media, which he claimed was an attempt to tarnish his image as one of the lawyers representing the politician.
Mazery, who is now the head of Investigation Branch B in the MACC's Investigation Division, subsequently apologised to the legal team, particularly Amer Hamzah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Company owner, car broker on remand for probe into falsification of vehicle ownership documents
Article:
IPOH: A company owner and a car broker are on remand for seven days until Sept 21 to assist in an investigation into a syndicate allegedly falsifying vehicle ownership documents at a local enforcement agency.
According to a source from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), the two men, in their 30s and 40s, respectively, are suspected of bribing officers at the agency to alter vehicle ownership records.
The source said magistrate S. S. Evangelin issued the remand order following an application by the MACC at the Magistrate's Court here this morning.
The two suspects were detained yesterday while they were at the Perak MACC office to have their statements recorded.
The arrests followed the MACC's uncovering of the syndicate's activities in collaboration with the Road Transport Department (RTD), which allegedly involved falsifying vehicle ownership documents to facilitate changes in ownership status.
Perak MACC director Azizul Ahmad Sarkawi confirmed the remand when contacted, saying the case was being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Enforcement agency personnel among four remanded over animal feed claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An enforcement agency personnel was among four people remanded for five days for allegedly submitting false documents in claims involving the supply of animal feed worth RM1.8 million.
Magistrate Aina Azahra Ariffin ordered the four to be remanded until Saturday (Sept 19) following a MACC application at the magistrate's court today.
A source said the suspects, comprising three men and a woman aged between 40 and 60, were detained at about 9pm yesterday after appearing at the Kuala Lumpur MACC office to give statements.
The other three suspects were a retired enforcement agency staff, and the director and administrative manager of a private company.
The source said preliminary investigations found that the four allegedly conspired to commit the offence between 2021 and 2023.
"All four are believed to have submitted documents containing false details in claims for animal feed supplies worth about RM1.8 million, although the actual value of the supplies was lower," the source said.
Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib confirmed the arrests when contacted, saying the case was being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-GC moves to block judicial review of 2024 diesel subsidy removal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC)  has objected to an application by two men seeking leave for a judicial review of the government's decision to remove and rationalise diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in June 2024.
Senior federal counsel Mohammad Sallehuddin Md Ali contended that the decision to end the subsidies cannot be challenged through judicial review, as the matter is not governed by any written law.
"The granting or withdrawal of subsidies is not a right provided under the law; rather, it is a form of financial assistance and a policy decision that the court cannot adjudicate," he said during the hearing of the leave application today.
Mohammad Sallehuddin also argued that the court need not examine the issue at all, since it had become academic after diesel prices and subsidy methods were standardised nationwide on July 1 last year.
The application for leave to commence judicial review was filed on Oct 7, 2024, by Azhani Marlan @ Abd Halim, 49, and Mohd Hatta Sanuri, 50.
They named Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also finance minister, former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and the government as the first to sixth respondents.
The two men are seeking, among other things, a declaration that the defendants' decision on June 9, 2024, to scrap the diesel subsidy and set the retail price at RM3.35 per litre, up from RM2.15, a 56 per cent jump, is null and void in law.
The move took effect on June 10, 2024, in Peninsular Malaysia, with Sabah and Sarawak exempted.
Meanwhile, the applicants' lawyer Mohaji Selamat argued that the decision is amenable to judicial review because it involves neither national security nor any specific prerogative power that is ordinarily non-justiciable.
"The government's decision on diesel subsidies is subject to the law, including Article 8 of the Federal Constitution and Section 6(2)(g) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961.
"Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution states that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to equal protection of the law. So why are people in Peninsular Malaysia denied the subsidy when, at the time, unlimited subsidies were given to Sabah and Sarawak?" he said.
Mohaji said the issue should not be dismissed as academic merely because the government is restoring diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in stages.
He asserted that a judicial review application can still proceed even if the decision being challenged has been withdrawn or changed.
"In our view, the damage or impact arising from that decision, from June 10, 2024, until July 1, 2026, does not disappear simply because the subsidy has been reinstated," he said.
After hearing submissions from both sides, Judge Norliza Othman fixed Nov 16 for the decision on the application for leave to commence judicial review.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 80.35kg syabu disguised as 'tofu cat litter' seized in Bintulu
Article:
BINTULU: An attempt to smuggle 80.35kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.01 million through a courier service, disguised as packages declared as 'tofu cat litter', was foiled by the Customs Department in Sarawak.
Sarawak Customs director Datuk Norizan Haji Yahya said the seizure was carried out by the Bintulu Enforcement Branch in collaboration with the Narcotics Branch and Intelligence Branch at the department's headquarters.
He said officers began monitoring several packages addressed to a premises in Bintulu on Aug 28.
"The packages were declared as tofu cat litter, but were suspected to contain drugs.
"Monitoring and surveillance were carried out for 12 days, but no one came forward to claim the packages," he said in a statement today.
He said subsequent inspection found that the packages contained methamphetamine.
Norizan said the use of non-existent recipient details was believed to be an attempt to prevent the shipment from being traced by the authorities.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Joint commission meet with Maldives proposed in Kuala Lumpur by year-end
Article:
MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed that the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission meet in Kuala Lumpur by the end of the year, signalling a push to accelerate bilateral cooperation and resolve outstanding issues between the two countries.
Anwar said the commission was "very, very critical," particularly as several matters remained unresolved, and that an early meeting would demonstrate both countries' commitment to strengthening their bilateral ties.
"I then propose that the joint commission between the two countries be facilitated at the earliest possible time, and we can even explore the possibility of having the meeting, which we will host in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year," he said in a joint press conference here, today.
Anwar began his two-day visit to the Maldives with a ceremonial welcome in Male on Monday, as Malaysia seeks to deepen ties with the Indian Ocean archipelago across trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, arrived at the presidential Izzudheen Jetty, at 9.29am local time (12.29pm Malaysia), where he was received by President Dr Mohamed Muizzu and welcomed with a cultural performance by local schoolchildren.
He was accompanied by Maldives' Islamic Affairs Minister Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, the minister-in-attendance for the visit.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam were also present.
Anwar said stronger bilateral relations should be built on mutual understanding, respect and trust at both personal and national levels.
"That would showcase our commitment to enhance bilateral relations between our two brotherly and sisterly countries," he said.
He said the proposed mechanism could also help address issues involving the two countries' embassies and other matters requiring government-to-government coordination.
Anwar said Malaysia and the Maldives had developed a close relationship and expressed appreciation for President Mohamed Muizzu's commitment to strengthening ties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar praises Maldivian president for taking principled stand on Palestine
Article:
MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim praised Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu for taking a principled stand on the Palestinian issue, saying Malaysia and the Maldives shared broadly similar foreign policy positions, particularly on Gaza.
He said both countries remained deeply concerned over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where the killings and destruction of Palestinians had continued despite calls for human rights and democracy by the international community.
"I appreciate the stance taken by the president and the motive in government, and we will continue to do our move to assist because this is an issue not only close our hearts, but it's justice and freedom," Anwar said in a joint press conference with Muizzu, here, today.
He said the international community must also confront the issue of colonisation in Palestine, noting that countries which had fought against colonialism were now reluctant to speak out against Israel's occupation of Palestinian land.
"Yesterday, I mentioned the term colonisation. We all fought against colonisation. But when it comes to Palestine, being colonised by Israel, not many are prepared to speak up and demand (justice)," he said.
Addressing Muizzu directly, Anwar said the Maldivian leader represented "one voice of reason and conscience" and described him as a true defender of human rights and freedom.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: People advised against rushing to replace MyKad from Sept 17
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions.
"I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad. There are currently 24 million MyKad cards in circulation, with an average of 180,000 to 200,000 cards issued each month," he told reporters today.
He said the replacement of the MyKad would not affect subsidy balances or eligibility for subsidies linked to the identity card.
"There is no issue regarding the subsidy balance...the records are based on the existing MyKad," he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin said the department handles between 13,000 and 15,000 cases of unregistered births each year, a figure he described as still high even though Malaysia gained independence decades ago.
He said failure to register births was due to various factors, including lack of information, social problems and family issues, which could ultimately affect the children's future.
"The reality is that there are still people who lack the basic knowledge that every birth must be registered, and this is still regarded as something normal," he said, adding that parents or guardians gave various reasons for failing to register their children's births, including financial difficulties and family constraints, even though birth registration is free.
In this regard, he urged parents, guardians and the public with information on unregistered births to come forward to NRD offices for assistance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang litterbugs plead to avoid community service
Article:
KUANTAN: They were ordered to clean up their act — literally — but some litterbugs in Pahang have instead turned up at the solid waste management office, pleading to be spared community service.
The offenders, including civil servants and professionals, have attempted to negotiate with the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp), with some even offering to pay a higher fine instead of performing community service.
But the SWCorp enforcement team is having none of it.
SWCorp Pahang director Cairul Hisham Jalaluddin said a total of 3,295 notices had been issued across Pahang between Jan 1 and Sept 14 this year, with about 200 offenders ordered to perform community service.
"There were some who turned up at our office attempting to negotiate and offered to pay a higher fine instead of performing community service. We explained that the Community Service Order is mandatory and those who fail to comply will face a heavier fine of up to RM10,000.
"For many, they seem unperturbed about paying the fine and their concern is having to perform community service, including cleaning drains and sweeping litter at public places such as recreational parks," he told reporters at the 50th SWCorp Pahang CSO programme at Taman Gelora here today.
The programme today involved 22 offenders performing community service in four districts — Kuantan, Bera, Pekan and Temerloh.
The offenders, aged between 19 and 68, were ordered to perform between two and four hours of community service under the supervision of SWCorp team members.
Cairul Hisham said offenders across Pahang included foreigners, professionals, civil servants, students and retirees, with some aged above 70.
Meanwhile, he said he had noticed a drop in littering cases over the past few months since the new anti-littering law took effect this year, particularly at rest and service areas and outside shopping malls.
"Our plainclothes enforcement officers deployed to catch litterbugs in public areas have reported that the majority of individuals now discard their cigarette butts in rubbish bins.
"There have also been viral videos on social media showing our enforcement team issuing notices to those who litter in public areas, so this may have instilled some fear among potential offenders. As a result, they find the nearest rubbish bin to dispose of the waste, including cigarette butts," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOF seizes smuggled cigarettes worth over RM1.9mil in Klang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized various types of smuggled cigarettes, worth over RM1.9 million, in a raid on a premises in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang yesterday.
Its 4th Battalion commanding officer, Supt Amanjit Singh, said the raid under Op Taring Alpha 1, conducted at 4.30pm by its intelligence branch in Semenyih, with the assistance of the North Klang District Criminal Investigation Division (BSJD).
He said that during the raid, the police arrested a 52-year-old man who was suspected of being the courier for the untaxed cigarettes supply.
As a result of the raid, the police seized a total of 4,920 cartons of various types and brands of untaxed cigarettes.
"Also seized was a Nissan Almera car suspected to be used in the distribution of the cigarettes, with a total estimated seizure value of RM1,907,163.20," he said in a statement today.
He said the case is being investigated under the Customs Act 1967, while the suspect and all the seized goods have been taken to the Klang Utara district police headquarters for further action.
Meanwhile, he urged the community to continue cooperating and providing any information to the police regarding illegal activities in their area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Residential projects built in Melaka to undergo selling price valuation review
Article:
MELAKA: The state government will ensure that every new development, especially residential projects built in Melaka, undergoes a review of the selling price valuation before the project is implemented.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the review will be conducted by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) through the State Land Subdivision and Partition Committee.
He said that the effort needs to be made so that the development carried out is in line with economic growth, job opportunities, housing needs and the people's financial capacity.
"For me, this is not just about the process or approval, but we want the price (of the residence) brought to the market to be truly reasonable, in line with the current value, and still within the reach of buyers.
"The proof, Alhamdulillah, based on the National Property Information Centre Report for the first quarter of this year, Melaka recorded the lowest house sale prices in Malaysia," he said.
He said this while delivering a speech at the inauguration of the Best Data Supplier Appreciation Ceremony of the National Property Information Centre (NAPIC) and the What's New Property Information System Malaysia 2.0 Southern Zone Seminar, which was also attended by JPPH director-general Datuk Abdul Razak Yusak.
Ab Rauf said that in the first six months of this year, Melaka recorded 8,661 real estate transactions worth RM3.1 billion, with the residential subsector remaining the main contributor via 5,479 transactions worth RM1.78 billion.
He said the housing affordability ratio in Melaka is around 3.27 compared to the national average of 4.39, but this achievement is not a licence for the state government to feel complacent.
He also said the challenge that needs to be faced is ensuring that the level of affordability can be maintained as the market, development costs, and people's needs continue to change.
"The state government aims to increase the home ownership rate to 88 per cent by 2030, and we want more people in Melaka not just to dream of owning a home, but to finally hold the keys to their own house.
"For me, that is the true measure of the success of a housing policy, not how many houses we approve or build, but how many people can truly afford to own them," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police open to helping MOH operate mercy flights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The police are open to helping the Health Ministry (MOH) operate mercy flights to transport patients requiring emergency treatment from remote areas.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said the air operations force currently faced constraints in terms of available air assets, given the vast operational area it covered nationwide.
He said the police currently had only two fixed-wing aircraft and one helicopter available in Sarawak.
"While the need may be quite urgent at this moment, I believe this is something we can consider for the future and to foster better cooperation with the ministry concerned.
"Perhaps through the acquisition of new assets or other means, we can facilitate collaboration between the ministry and agencies to ensure that their duties and responsibilities are carried out more effectively in the future," he said.
He said this at a press conference after the Senior Police Officer Rank Insignia Presentation and Handover of Duties Ceremony at the Kuala Lumpur Police Training Centre (Pulapol) here today.
It was previously reported that Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies would assist MOH in operating mercy flights to ensure residents in remote areas requiring medical treatment continued to have access to healthcare services.
The temporary mercy flight services will be provided pending completion of the investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Miri, Sarawak, on Sept 8, in which the aircraft caught fire.
On the progress of the crash investigation, Khalid expressed his condolences to the victims' families and said police had so far recorded statements from 20 witnesses.
He said additional statements would be recorded before the investigation papers were completed.
Meanwhile, Khalid said police were finalising their investigation into a report lodged by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, who claimed he had been coerced into signing the Proclamation Instrument seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
He said the matter was sensitive and required thorough scrutiny, taking into account not only the police investigation but also the customs and traditions of Negri Sembilan.
"We are still preparing the investigation papers and may require further action, as well as input from the Attorney General's Chambers and other relevant parties," he said.
Ismail had claimed he was forced to sign the document before lodging a police report on Sept 8 to enable the authorities to investigate the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must strengthen care economy to boost women's workforce participation - Nancy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must strengthen its care economy to help more women enter or return to the workforce, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
Delivering her keynote address at the 5th Malaysia Sustainability Leadership Summit today, she said 42.8 per cent of the 4.89 million women outside the labour force cited domestic responsibilities and caregiving as their main reason for staying out of the workforce.
She said that caregiving had long been treated as a private family matter, borne disproportionately by women and often without formal recognition, training or adequate support.
"Nearly one million women in Malaysia are both the primary caregiver and sole breadwinner in their households. Many are single mothers, and only a proportion are connected to formal social protection systems.
"This is not a question of talent or capability. It is a structural gap that prevents our economy from fully benefiting from women's skills and potential," she said.
She said the issue was reflected in Malaysia's female labour force participation rate, which stood at 56.6 per cent in 2025, significantly lower than the 83.3 per cent recorded for men.
She said the figures showed that more needs to be done to remove barriers preventing women from participating fully in the labour market, particularly those related to caregiving responsibilities.
"Malaysia cannot realise its full economic potential while half of its talent pool remains underutilised. Hence, women's economic participation remains a major opportunity," she said.
She said the ministry is implementing the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan 2026–2030 as a national roadmap to professionalise, regulate and expand a sustainable care ecosystem.
She said the framework sets out the strategic direction for improving the quality, affordability and accessibility of childcare and eldercare, while strengthening recognition and training for caregivers.
"A well-structured care economy can create quality employment, professionalise caregiving, support women who wish to enter or return to the workforce, and open new opportunities for social enterprises and businesses."
Nancy said addressing the issue also requires stronger collaboration between the government, businesses, civil society, communities and academia through a Public-Private-People Partnership (4P).
She emphasised that businesses should increasingly view family-friendly policies, care infrastructure and flexible work arrangements as investments in productivity, talent retention and sustainable business performance, rather than mere corporate social responsibility initiatives.
Furthermore, she said Malaysia's ageing population, evolving family structures and changing economic pressures on households require more urgent and precise responses.
She called on organisations participating in the summit to identify at least one concrete cross-sector collaboration arising from the event, with clear deliverables and measurable outcomes for the year ahead.
The 5th Malaysia Sustainability Leadership Summit convened about 130 policymakers, government officials, business and sustainability leaders, civil society representatives and community leaders to strengthen collaboration and speed up Malaysia's progress towards the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi presents Malaysia Day invitation to Sarawak governor
Article:
KUCHING: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today paid a courtesy call on Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar to present an official invitation to the Malaysia Day celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) tomorrow night.
Fahmi said the visit also provided an opportunity to brief Wan Junaidi on final preparations for the celebration, which is scheduled to run from 8.15pm to about 10.30pm.
"Alhamdulillah, the courtesy call went very well. Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah and I presented the invitation to Tun for tomorrow's celebration.
"All preparations are progressing well. There are a few technical aspects that will be fine-tuned and, insya-Allah, the event will run smoothly," he told reporters after the courtesy call at Astana Negeri Sarawak.
Also present were Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister and Minister-in-Charge of the Malaysia Day 2026 celebration Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, and Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Fahmi said that during the hour-long meeting, Wan Junaidi also shared some of his extensive experience, particularly from his time serving in the police.
Fahmi said he also updated Wan Junaidi on the publication of a special book about the Governor by the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), as well as several related programmes, including a thanksgiving ceremony at the State Mosque and a Malaysia Day exhibition organised by the Information Department.
About 5,000 people are expected to attend the Malaysia Day celebration at BCCK tomorrow night.
Wan Junaidi and his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi, are expected to attend, along with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia agrees in principle to support Maldives’ US$100m soft loan request, says Anwar
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia has agreed in principle to support the Maldives’ application for a US$100 million (US$1=RM4.07) financing facility, which Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through both countries’ monetary authorities.
Anwar said that the terms and mechanism for the facility are still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA).
He said that in principle, Malaysia has no issue with the application, taking into account the Maldives’ repayment record and the cooperation between the two countries, as well as the government guarantee that would need to be provided.
“It is essentially a soft loan, but it will be carried out through Bank Negara and the financial authorities.
“As for the terms, these are still being examined by both central banks, although in principle we have no issue with their repayment record, as well as the cooperation and government guarantee that must be in place,” he told the Malaysian media after concluding his official visit to the country.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
Earlier, at a joint press conference with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, Anwar said the Maldivian leader had raised the matter with him and had also written regarding the need for BNM to respond to the MMA’s request for the US$100 million facility.
“The President has written to me about the need to get our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, to respond to the Maldivian request, precisely (from) the Maldives Monetary Authority, for this US$100 million facility.
“We have agreed in principle to support this, although both the central bank and MMA will have to work in the fastest time possible on the mechanism and the process to ensure that the agreement can be settled in the fastest time possible. And this can only be done based on trust and friendship,” he said.
The Prime Minister is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives and held a four-eye meeting and bilateral talks with Muizzu today. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia, Maldives to expand cooperation in maritime security, halal and haj
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia and the Maldives are set to expand cooperation in maritime security and training, as well as halal, wakaf and haj, following the exchange of two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on defence and Islamic affairs today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that as a maritime nation, the Maldives placed particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training.
“The Maldives is a maritime nation and places great importance on maritime cooperation, as well as cooperation in security, training and maritime safety and security, which we will continue to pursue,” he told Malaysian media after completing his official programme at the President’s Office here today.
On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives’ status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj.
Earlier, Anwar and Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu witnessed the exchange of the two cooperation documents at the President’s Office.
At a joint press conference later, Muizzu said the agreements opened new avenues for practical cooperation while strengthening the institutional foundations of Malaysia-Maldives bilateral relations.
“Today we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.
“These agreements open new avenues for practical cooperation and further strengthen the institutional foundations of our bilateral relationship,” he said.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
Anwar is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives, which ends this afternoon. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Prosecution completes case after 29 witnesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The prosecution today completed its case in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse trial after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses, which means that the trial will now move on to the next stage.
Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin this afternoon told the High Court that the prosecution closes its case, and that the prosecution will offer six witnesses that Muhyiddin could call in as his witnesses if he is ordered to defend himself in this case.
"With that, the prosecution closes this case. I offer the following witnesses," he said, while listing the potential witnesses and promising to help call in those witnesses if required by Muhyiddin.
The six are Muhyiddin's then deputy chief private secretary Asmar Asmadi Abdullah Sani, Muhyiddin's former principal private secretary Datuk Marzuki Mohamad, Datuk Mohd Ayob Mohd Ali, former Treasury secretary-general Datuk Seri Asri Hamidon, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer Mohd Syahmeizy Sulong, and Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin then scheduled four days for continued hearing, namely November 26, December 1 to 3.
When the trial resumes in November and December, the prosecution and Muhyiddin's lawyers are expected to present their arguments on whether Muhyiddin will have to enter his defence in this case.
There are two stages in a criminal trial, with the prosecution having to prove that it has shown a prima facie case after calling in all the prosecution witnesses.
After hearing the arguments from both sides, the High Court will decide whether there is a prima facie case.
If the High Court finds there is no prima facie case, Muhyiddin would be acquitted.
If the High Court decides there is a prima facie case, the trial would move on to the defence stage where Muhyiddin would be ordered to defend himself.
Muhyiddin's trial started on March 9, and has gone on for about 32 days now.
Earlier today, the prosecution applied for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA) for four of the seven charges that Muhyiddin is facing in this trial, with the High Court then exercising its discretion under the law to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges in the interests of justice.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).

Title: Four of seven missing anglers found safe off Sekinchan, search continues for three
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 15 — Four of the seven anglers reported missing yesterday were found safe by a local fishing boat in the waters off Sekinchan, 25 nautical miles from the coast of Sungai Besar, at about 9.50 am today.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the four men were found floating close to one another and were in a weak condition.
“They are now receiving treatment at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR), Klang, and Banting Hospital, Kuala Langat, while the cause of the incident is still under investigation.
“Hazy conditions reduced visibility and made the SAR operation slightly more challenging,” he said in a statement.
He said the search and rescue operation was ongoing to locate the remaining three victims, with the maritime search area expanded to 203.5 square nautical miles, while the aerial search covers 764 square nautical miles.
He said the second day of the SAR operation involved MMEA sea and air assets, as well as assets from the Royal Malaysia Police, Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force and two local fishing boats.
“MMEA will continue to coordinate the search efforts with the agencies involved to ensure the SAR operation is carried out comprehensively and continuously until all the victims are located.
“Any information related to the incident can be channelled to Selangor MMEA at 013-660 6652,” he added.
Six anglers and a boat skipper were reported missing after they could not be located in the waters off One Fathom Bank, near Pulau Ketam. — Bernama

Title: Babysitter pleads not guilty to exposing toddler to conditions that could have caused death
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — A babysitter pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of exposing a 13-month-old boy under her care to conditions that could have caused his death last week.
Noraidah Khairuddin, 44, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Irwan Suainbon.
According to the charge, Noraidah, as a person having custody of the toddler, was accused of exposing him in a manner that could have caused his death.
“I plead not guilty because I did not do anything to him,” she said.
The offence was allegedly committed at a house in Taman Desa Mawar, Lintang Kampung Melayu 2, Air Itam, at 2 pm on Sept 8.
She was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor M Darrshini offered bail of RM20,000 with one surety, along with conditions that the accused report to a nearby police station on the first of every month and refrain from tampering with the prosecution witnesses.
The accused’s lawyer, Naqieya Zulkernain of the National Legal Aid Foundation, sought a reduction in bail on the grounds that her client is a housewife who depends on her husband, who has no fixed income, and that they have three children.
The court granted bail of RM8,000 with one surety, along with the additional conditions requested by the prosecution and fixed case mention for Nov 16, pending the post-mortem report.
On Sept 10, police detained Noraidah and the boy’s mother to assist investigations after he was found unconscious with bluish lips at the babysitter’s home in Air Itam. — Bernama

Title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as safety points to boost crime prevention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The Kuala Lumpur Police propose making KK Mart convenience stores as Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations through a strategic collaboration with the company to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital.
Its chief, Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team has identified around 700 KK Mart branches in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor that operate 24 hours, have bright lighting, and are equipped with centralised closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, which have the potential to be safe locations for the public to seek assistance during emergencies.
“We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. At the same time, we will enhance cooperation in terms of patrolling and monitoring so that these premises become safe places for the public,” he said.
He said this to reporters at the press conference for the opening of the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent headquarters (IPK) today, which was also attended by KK Supermart & Superstore Sdn Bhd founder and executive chairman Datuk Seri Dr Chai Kee Kan.
Fadil said that they are also looking into the possibility of being granted access to the centralised CCTV of the convenience store chain, which simultaneously strengthens security monitoring in the surrounding area.
According to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the GTSP programme is an initiative that creates a network of strategic partner premises as safety points for the public to obtain immediate assistance in the event of an emergency, a crime, or a security threat.
Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur IPK is the first convenience store branch in the PDRM building. and there may be more opened in PDRM buildings that will benefit the police personnel and the local community.
Commenting on the control of goods sold at the KK Mart premises in the Kuala Lumpur IPK, he said that the business operations are subject to government premises regulations, and any prohibited goods will not be allowed for sale.
Meanwhile, Chai said that there are currently around 1,100 KK Mart branches nationwide, and he sees great potential to place the convenience store in government buildings.
He also welcomed KK Mart’s initiative as a GTSP and was willing to share CCTV footage from the convenience store chain to assist PDRM investigations. —Bernama

Title: Anwar moots Malaysia-Maldives joint commission in KL this year
Article:
MALÉ, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed convening the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year to further advance bilateral relations between the two countries.
Anwar said the Commission would be an important platform to address outstanding issues and translate the close relationship between Malaysia and the Maldives into concrete cooperation.
He said bilateral ties must be built on a sincere appreciation of each other’s needs and strengths, underpinned by mutual respect and trust at both the leadership and country-to-country levels.
“That is why, when the President showed such fondness and commitment, I then proposed that the Joint Commission between the two countries be facilitated at the earliest possible time.
“We will host it in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year. And that will showcase our commitment to enhance bilateral relations between our two brotherly and sisterly countries,” he said this at a joint press conference with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu at the President’s Office here today.
Anwar said the Commission could also address issues affecting Maldivians in Malaysia, including students and those seeking healthcare.
More than 2,000 Maldivian students were studying in Malaysia, reflecting not only the friendship between the two countries but also Maldivians’ confidence in Malaysia’s education system, he noted.
He said there were some bureaucratic issues involving parents accompanying their children studying in Malaysia, which he had discussed with his colleagues and hoped could be addressed at the next Cabinet meeting.
“I don’t think this is an issue of policy differences. We don’t have problems with Maldivians living in Malaysia, working in Malaysia, or even studying in Malaysia. So I think we will showcase this and respond positively,” the Prime Minister said.
On healthcare, Anwar said issues involving a small number of Maldivians requiring assistance should be resolved promptly, in keeping with the compassion and caring values underpinning the MADANI framework. — Bernama

Title: Don’t rush: Home minister urges Malaysians to avoid MyKad replacement frenzy
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions.
“I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad. There are currently 24 million MyKad cards in circulation, with an average of 180,000 to 200,000 cards issued each month,” he told reporters here today.
He said the replacement of the MyKad would not affect subsidy balances or eligibility for subsidies linked to the identity card.
“There is no issue regarding the subsidy balance...the records are based on the existing MyKad,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said the department handles between 13,000 and 15,000 cases of unregistered births each year, a figure he described as still high even though Malaysia gained independence decades ago.
He said failure to register births was due to various factors, including lack of information, social problems and family issues, which could ultimately affect the children’s future.
