“The reality is that there are still people who lack the basic knowledge that every birth must be registered, and this is still regarded as something normal,” he said, adding that parents or guardians gave various reasons for failing to register their children’s births, including financial difficulties and family constraints, even though birth registration is free.
In this regard, he urged parents, guardians and members of the public with information on unregistered births to come forward to NRD offices for assistance. — Bernama

Title: Prosecution drops four charges against Muhyiddin, presses on with three in corruption trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now.
In this trial, Muhyiddin faced seven charges:
four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and
three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
Following the High Court's decision after the prosecution's request for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA), Muhyiddin now only faces three power abuse charges involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin delivered her decision this afternoon on whether to only grant a DNAA or to acquit Muhyiddin on those four charges.
Ultimately, the judge decided to acquit, in the interests of justice.
Just before lunch break today, deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib informed the High Court that the prosecution had decided to not continue with four of the seven charges in Muhyiddin's trial, saying this was after the prosecution had looked at the case as a whole.
"With that, the prosecution respectfully applies for Section 254(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code to be applied, to apply for an order from this court for a DNAA on the accused. We apply for DNAA only on those charges," he said.
Muhyiddin's lawyers had however urged the High Court to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges related to Bukhary Equity, instead of only granting a DNAA.
MORE TO COME

Title: Ipsos poll: Malaysians prioritise jobs and homes over traditional milestones
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Malaysians largely mirror global views on success, prioritising stable employment and home ownership, yet they place a significantly higher premium on marriage and parenthood as life milestones, according to a new Ipsos report.
The Ipsos Life Aspirations 2026 report reveals that two in three Malaysians view stability and security as the primary markers of a successful life. Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent.
The findings, based on a survey of 501 Malaysians aged 18 to 74, highlight a clear cultural emphasis on family.
Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent.
However, a generational divide is emerging. While the fundamentals of success remain broadly similar, Gen Z Malaysians are placing less emphasis on traditional family milestones than their Millennial counterparts.
Both generations agree on the primacy of career stability, with 69 per cent of Millennials and 68 per cent of Gen Z citing a full-time, stable job as the most important marker of success. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.
The gap in family aspirations is more pronounced: only 32 per cent of Gen Z respondents view marriage as a marker of success, compared to 58 per cent of Millennials. Similarly, only 35 per cent of Gen Z value parenthood as a milestone, against 50 per cent of Millennials.
Ipsos Malaysia managing director Arun Menon noted that this shift aligns with wider demographic trends, as Malaysians increasingly delay marriage and parenthood in favour of education, career progression, and financial security.
The most striking disparity, however, lies in home ownership. While 79 per cent of respondents aspire to own a home, only 46 per cent have achieved this goal, underscoring the persistent affordability crisis in the local housing market.
“Around three in four Malaysians aspire to own a home, yet fewer than half have achieved it, echoing the wider affordability challenges in Malaysia’s housing market,” Arun said.
He added that these findings suggest younger Malaysians are not necessarily redefining success, but are instead reordering their priorities, securing financial and personal stability before pursuing traditional life milestones.

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Lawyer accuses MACC officer of ‘intimidation’ over police report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report.
Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information.
Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.
Amer said the MACC officer who lodged the police report had said he received information from the investigating officer in Muhyiddin’s trial, adding that he could only infer that it refers to Mazery who is still under oath and was scheduled to give evidence in court today.
“It’s clearly an attempt at intimidation,” he said. “But I’m not intimidated, they drew first blood and I will repay them with no quarters.”
Amer accused Mazery of trying to tarnish his reputation and trying to mislead the public via the police report’s claim that the document is not related to Muhyiddin’s trial, describing it as an “underhanded tactic” by a witness who was still testifying in court.
The alleged classified document was the statement that MACC had recorded from Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad during investigations.
“No court should condone this kind of tactic. Yang Arif is supposed to decide on subject matter of the case based on all facts and legal arguments. Yet the very IO whom we have challenged with several issues, decided to undermine the entire trial process by lodging this report,” he said.
Amer told the High Court that he is considering various legal action: “I will not exclude the possibility of lodging a report against the appropriate person including the IO for making false report, contempt of court and any other legal action. I reserve all those rights.”
“I’m making an application to this court to reserve my right to further cross this witness with regard to his underhanded tactic,” he added.
Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex September 2, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik said the defence team stands in support of Amer, while fellow defence lawyer Datuk Seri K. Kumaraendran asked if the High Court would consider commencing contempt of court proceedings against Mazery.
Mazery then apologised to Amer and explained the police report made by his MACC colleague was only intended to ensure that there had been no leaks of classified information.
“First, I want to apologise to the lawyers, especially Datuk Amer, about the issue of report lodged. About that report, actually I worried that the document came from MACC officers, so I worried there is a leak of internal information from MACC officers. If there is, I have to protect my department, MACC’s integrity.
“That’s why the report was made to see if there was leaks from MACC itself. So we don’t want this classified document that is so important could simply go out, especially in the future,” he said, adding that he has no intention to hurt the image of the lawyers whom he had always respected.
Mazery said he may get the police report withdrawn if he finds there were no leaks by MACC officers.
After hearing Mazery’s explanation, Amer stressed that the document was provided by the prosecution to Adam Radlan’s lawyers in the latter’s own case, and that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had obtained the document from Adam Radlan’s lawyers.
“To clear the air, we obtained this document from the legal team representing Adam Radlan, we never obtained this document through any illegal or improper channels. So let it be clear, that the report has no basis whatsoever,” he said, adding that Mazery could have asked him first where the document came from instead of lodging the police report.
“I never obtained it from MACC, we never obtained it from MACC, 100 per cent,” Amer later said at another point, also adding that Muhyiddin’s lawyers are “entitled” to obtain it from Adam Radlan’s lawyers as they feel it is relevant to Muhyiddin’s trial.
While taking note of Mazery’s apology and explanation, Amer said he still reserves his rights and that his reputation remains tarnished for every second that the police report remains out there.
Amer had pointed out that the police report had been reported by the media.
After Muhyiddin’s lawyer Rosli Dahlan pressed for Mazery to inform the court that the police report would be withdrawn, the judge allowed Mazery’s request to carry out the necessary checks before withdrawing the report and also directed him to report to the court as soon as possible.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume this afternoon, with Mazery expected to update the court on the status of the police report.

Title: Police receive two reports over Negeri Sembilan MB’s alleged forced signing of royal document
Article:
SEREMBAN,  Sept 15 — Police have received two reports concerning the Proclamation document allegedly signed under duress by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said following the reports lodged by the Menteri Besar, the police would classify the case to determine the appropriate direction and scope of the investigation.
“I can confirm that two police reports were lodged by the Menteri Besar. It is our duty, upon receiving the reports, to classify them based on the nature and direction of the investigation.
“I leave it to the wisdom of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to handle the complaint,” he told reporters here today.
He was met after presenting a sponsored Umrah package to Nurul Arini Abdullah, 19, who was among those assisted by the National Registration Department (JPN) in obtaining her identity card last year, and her mother, Norini Basir, 62, here today.
Saifuddin Nasution advised the public to respect the rule of law and refrain from making assumptions that could disrupt the investigation or public order.
Ismail had previously claimed that he was forced to sign the document before lodging a police report on Sept 8 to facilitate an investigation by the authorities.
Media reports previously quoted Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as saying that the allegation needed to be verified by the lawyer who was present during the signing process.
The UMNO president also said the party would not interfere in the matter, but fully respected the royal institution, laws and customs of Negeri Sembilan. — Bernama

Title: Pesta Pulau Pinang returns, but moves to Tasek Gelugor after 50 Years at Sungai Nibong
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — Pesta Pulau Pinang will return this year for a month-long celebration starting December 1, with the event relocating to Padang Menora in Tasek Gelugor.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow confirmed that while the annual event continues as scheduled, it will be held at a more compact venue compared to its traditional site in Sungai Nibong.
“Although Padang Menora is smaller than the Sungai Nibong grounds, it is suitable for continuing the annual event,” Chow told reporters following the closing ceremony of the national-level Penang2030 public speaking competition at USM today.
The decision to move the event follows the closure of the original Pesta grounds to facilitate the construction of the Mutiara Line light rail transit (LRT) station and depot.
The state government had explored several alternative locations before the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) offered the Tasek Gelugor site.
Despite the change in venue, the state executive council decided to retain the name “Pesta Pulau Pinang,” acknowledging the brand’s prestige and recognition over the past half-century.
The event will run from December 1 to 31, with further details to be announced once finalised.
The former Pesta site in Sungai Nibong is now the focus of a proposed Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Masterplan covering approximately 23.47 hectares.
Developed through a collaboration between the state government, the Asian Development Bank, MRT Corporation, and various federal and state agencies, the draft master plan is expected to be finalised in October.
The vision for the site is to create a long-term, mixed-use transit hub integrating residential, commercial, and public facilities. This large-scale urban transformation is expected to take between 10 and 15 years to fully implement.

Title: Fadhlina urges parents to screen children early for autism, ADHD and learning difficulties
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) is encouraging parents to bring their children for screening programmes aimed at detecting learning difficulties, including autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), at an early stage.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the screening programmes are crucial to ensuring children with learning difficulties receive appropriate intervention and support.
“Today, we are here to observe the intervention preparations put in place by the MOE to enable early detection of children with learning difficulties.
“Conditions such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD and others can be identified through these screening programmes. Therefore, these programmes are vital,” she told a press conference after attending the 2026 Parliamentary Follow-up Programme (Series 3) at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Gua Musang here today.
She said parents who noticed developmental delays or suspected undiagnosed learning difficulties in their children are encouraged to seek assessments from specialists provided by the ministry.
“We invite them to come to the Ministry of Education Malaysia, where we can conduct these assessments with the specialists available,” she said.
Fadhlina said the services include speech therapy and psychological assessments to evaluate children’s overall development.
“There is speech therapy, and psychologists will assess the children’s overall development and provide guidance and recommendations to parents on how to support their children’s learning process,” she said.
She stressed the importance of parental involvement, noting that the government provides the screening services free of charge.
“It is important for parents to take an active role, as the government provides these services for free.
“We therefore invite all parents to participate in these screenings so that our children can continue to receive the support they need,” she said.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said the ministry is prioritising literacy and numeracy proficiency among students, with efforts being strengthened at various levels through interventions and support from teachers and parents.
“We do not use the term ‘illiteracy’. Instead, we focus on strengthening literacy and numeracy proficiency at various levels,” she said.
She said the approach also covered Orang Asli children to ensure they did not fall behind and continued to receive priority and attention in education. — Bernama

Title: Anwar receives 21-gun salute as Maldives rolls out red carpet for Malaysian PM
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was accorded a full ceremonial welcome here today, marking the start of his official programme during his two-day visit to the Maldives.
Anwar arrived at the Presidential Jetty, the Izzudheen Jetty, here at 9.29 am local time (12.29 pm Malaysia time), where he was received by Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu and treated to a cultural performance by local schoolchildren.
The Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Maldives Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, who is the minister-in-attendance for the visit.
Also present at the welcoming ceremony were Malaysian Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
Anwar was then escorted to the saluting dais, where he received a salute from the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF), followed by a 21-gun salute.
Malaysia’s national anthem, Negaraku, was then played, followed by the Maldives’ national anthem, before Anwar inspected the guard of honour mounted by MNDF personnel.
After the inspection, the Prime Minister returned to the saluting dais to receive a second salute before he and Muizzu were introduced to members of both delegations.
The two leaders then walked about 150 metres from Republic Square to the President’s Office in a cultural procession accompanied by the beat of local drums and participants dressed in traditional Maldivian attire.
At the President’s Office, Anwar and Muizzu are scheduled to hold a four-eye meeting before leading their respective delegations in a bilateral meeting to discuss efforts to further strengthen Malaysia-Maldives relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The two leaders are also scheduled to witness the exchange of several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) before holding a joint press conference.
The visit reflects the commitment of both countries to further strengthen bilateral relations established in 1968, including in trade, investment and people-to-people ties. — Bernama

Title: Two detained after KPDN foils 2,400-litre diesel misappropriation attempt in Senai
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) foiled an attempt to misappropriate 2,400 litres of diesel in Ops Tiris 4.0 at a petrol station on Jalan Seelong, Senai, at about 2pm yesterday.
Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said the operation followed information and intelligence on diesel purchases suspected of violating the Control of Supplies Act 1961.
Enforcement personnel found a suspicious lorry equipped with a storage tank and related equipment, filling diesel directly into the tank.
“The lorry, four Intermediate Bulk Container (IBC) tanks, a flow meter, four pumps with hoses, two mobile phones and about 2,400 litres of liquid suspected to be diesel were seized. KPDN also seized 15 fleet cards and five receipts or invoices related to the fuel purchases,” Lilis Saslinda said in a statement.
Two local men in their 30s who were in the lorry were detained to assist investigations.
Document checks also found that the petrol station operator was suspected of committing an offence under Subregulation 12A of the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974.
Lilis Saslinda said the seized items were valued at about RM60,660 and the case was being investigated under Section 20(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961. — Bernama

Title: Police nab two ex-convicts in Johor over 11 cases involving housebreaking, robbery and theft
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 15 — Two ex-convicts who were released three years ago have been rearrested for their alleged involvement in 11 separate criminal cases, including housebreaking, robbery and theft, in the district recently.
Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the two male suspects, aged 26 and 27, were arrested in the Tanjung Kupang and Kangkar Pulai areas on Sept 5.
He said the arrests were made following a police report lodged on Sept 4 regarding a break-in at Forest City Starview in Gelang Patah.
“The two suspects, who hail from the northern states, were released from Pokok Sena Prison in Kedah back in 2023. They were previously incarcerated for criminal and drug-related offences.
“The suspects moved to Johor earlier this year to work in a factory, but were laid off in March and were later believed to be active in criminal activities,” he told reporters at the Iskandar Puteri district police headquarters here today.
Saifullah said initial investigations showed that the suspects were active during the early hours, targeting unoccupied homes and stealing postal parcels, including disposable diapers.
“The suspects were also believed to be responsible for a robbery at a data centre construction site in Gelang Patah on July 28, where they tied up the security guard before stealing copper cables worth RM50,000,” he said.
Following the arrests, Saifullah said investigators seized a laptop, three cameras, four mobile phones, copies of pawn tickets, copies of gold sale receipts and several other items.
In addition, he said police recovered two necklaces, five pairs of earrings, a Proton Waja, and two receipts for the sale of the copper.
“Investigators believe that the 26-year-old suspect, who had 11 prior criminal records, acted as the duo’s mastermind.
“His 27-year-old accomplice had 31 prior criminal records,” he said, adding that both men also tested positive for methamphetamine.
Investigations into the two suspects enabled police to solve several other cases involving housebreaking, breaking into a shophouse, a project site robbery, trespassing and postal parcel theft.
Both suspects have been remanded until Friday to assist with investigations under Sections 379, 457, 395 and 397 of the Penal Code.

Title: Lim Guan Eng’s call to drop Umno from Penang govt not DAP stance, says Chow Kon Yeow
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 15 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow stressed that DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government does not represent the party’s official position.
Kon Yeow said there had so far been no official directive from the party on the matter and that all parties should await a decision by the PH Presidential Council, according to a report published by
Harian Metro
.
He said statements issued by individuals at this point did not represent the party’s official position.
“It is not the party’s position (Lim Guan Eng’s challenge to Ahmad Zahid). For now, there are no party directives.
“Therefore, at this point, we stand by what has already been decided,” he told reporters when asked about the challenge and whether state PH would review its previous decision to accept cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) and Umno in the Penang state administration.
Elaborating, Kon Yeow, who is also chief minister, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook had issued a statement calling on Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to convene a PH Presidential Council meeting to discuss the coalition’s position on the matter.
As such, he said, all party leaders must abide by decisions made by the top leadership and refrain from issuing various statements that could cause confusion.
“We are bound by what is decided by the top leadership, not for individuals at lower levels to make various statements.
“We are focusing on the PH Presidential Council. As for the others, we will take note of them,” he said.
Earlier, Guan Eng challenged Ahmad Zahid to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government.
Guan Eng was reported to have said that Ahmad Zahid, who recently challenged the PH-led unity government to remove Umno from the Federal Government, should issue the same challenge in Penang.
Umno currently has representatives in the Penang State Executive Council (Exco), two city councils and state-linked companies.
He said PH could still retain a two-thirds majority in the Penang Legislative Assembly even without the two elected Umno representatives.
He alleged that Umno was taking advantage of what he described as the Penang PH leadership’s hesitation over its role in the state government, while at the same time working with Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Previous media reports said Umno had given the unity government an ultimatum to either hold the 16th General Election to seek a fresh mandate or officially remove Umno from the coalition.
Ahmad Zahid was reported to have said the demand was made after taking into account calls for Umno to no longer remain part of the unity government.

Title: Former construction manager claims trial over RM14,000 CBT involving Tabung Haji project
Article:
KOTA BHARU,  Sept  15 — A former construction project manager pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving penalty collection totalling RM14,000 from a contractor for a commercial building project owned by Lembaga Tabung Haji.
Mohamad Hashim Mukhatap, 53, then the Construction Manager for THP Timur Sdn Bhd, was charged with misappropriating the funds—collected as penalties from the contractor, Kelpile Sdn Bhd—by depositing them into his personal bank account.
The case involves a proposed project to construct and complete a 22-storey commercial building comprising serviced apartments (244 units), penthouses (four units), public amenities, commercial space, parking facilities, a sub-basement (one level), and related facilities on Lot 273, Section 12, Kota Bharu.
He allegedly committed the offence at Sofea Residensi, Lot 10015, Section 12 here, between Nov 15, 2017, and Aug 8, 2018.
The charge, framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Public Prosecutor Mariah Omar proposed bail at RM15,000, but defence counsel Fahmi Abd Moin Khairuddin requested that bail be set at RM5,000 for his client.
Judge Dazuki Ali allowed bail of RM8,000 with one surety and ordered the accused to surrender his passport, refrain from interfering with witnesses, and report to the MACC Shah Alam office monthly.
The court fixed Oct 19 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Four Chinese nationals claim trial over alleged kidnapping of woman in Alor Setar
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 15 — Three men and a woman, all of Chinese nationality, pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a fellow national last month.
Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 33; Guan Siqi, 24; and Liu Tingjun, 46, entered their pleas after the charge was read out to them in Mandarin before Judge N. Priscilla Hemamalini.
The four, together with another individual who was charged separately, allegedly kidnapped Xiong Xi Qiao, 33, with the intention of secretly and wrongfully confining her at a house in Taman Amira, Jalan Langgar, here at about 8.40 pm on Aug 7.
They were charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same law, which provides for a maximum of seven years’ imprisonment and a fine upon conviction.
The court denied them bail and set Oct 11 for mention.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nasruna Anhar Nordien appeared for the prosecution, while Guan Siqi was represented by lawyer S. Suresh, and the other three accused by lawyer Jodia Poh Yi Tying. — Bernama

Title: Queen Raja Zarith Sofiah orders postponement of Johor Family Day Carnival amid worsening haze
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, yesterday instructed that the Johor Family Day Carnival, scheduled for Sept 16, be postponed to a suitable date following the worsening haze situation in the state.
According to a post uploaded on the Facebook page of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar, Her Majesty instructed that the carnival be held when air quality improves.
“I advise the public to take precautionary measures, especially senior citizens and children, as well as those suffering from respiratory health problems.
“Although my intention is to provide a space for the people to create sweet memories in conjunction with Malaysia Day, we cannot take risks with the health of the people. Insya-Allah, this carnival will be held when air quality returns to a good level,” Her Majesty said.
The carnival, inspired by Her Majesty and organised by the state government and Yayasan Raja Zarith Sofiah Negeri Johor (YRZSNJ), gives the public an opportunity to enjoy themselves with their families and children in conjunction with Malaysia Day.
Several districts in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings today, including Johor Bahru, with readings as high as 162 in Pasir Gudang and 159 in Larkin. — Bernama

Title: Dzulkefly: 902 health clinics nationwide to offer AI-assisted lung screening by year-end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 902 health clinics nationwide will be empowered with Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted lung disease screening by the end of this year, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the initiative is part of the implementation of the 2025-2030 Lung Health Initiative to strengthen prevention, early detection, and management of respiratory diseases in the country.
“By the end of this year, 902 health clinics nationwide will be empowered with Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted screening, supported by the NALURY database,” he said via a post on Instagram yesterday.
Dzulkefly stated that this effort is also supported by the rigorous enforcement of the Public Health Smoking Product Control Act 2024 (Act 852), particularly to protect the younger generation from risks associated with the use of smoking products.
He said the step to strengthen lung health is crucial given that respiratory diseases currently account for one in five deaths globally.
“Recognising this reality, Malaysia continues to play a proactive role by championing an integrated lung health resolution at the 78th World Health Assembly (WHA), as well as elevating it as a key regional agenda during the recent 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM),” he said.
He noted that all efforts and innovations in this field must be supported by solid data and scientific evidence to ensure that implemented health policies and interventions are truly effective.
In this regard, Dr Dzulkefly praised the decade-long contributions of the NIHR Global Health Research Unit on Respiratory Health (RESPIRE) in driving public health research.
He also urged the research community to continue working closely with policymakers to ensure that scientific discoveries can be translated into effective clinical practices and public health interventions.
Dr Dzulkefly expressed his appreciation to Universiti Malaya, the University of Edinburgh, and all RESPIRE members for their continuous dedication in addressing global respiratory health challenges.
“Malaysia remains committed to forward-looking, evidence-driven, and solution-centric health policies,” he said after having officiated the 2026 RESPIRE Annual Scientific Meeting, which brought together over 100 international delegates in the capital. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Day H-series plate bidding opens tomorrow, numbers from 1 to 9,999 up for grabs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Bidding for the special H-series vehicle registration numbers in conjunction with Malaysia Day will open on Wednesday and run until Sept 20, offering numbers from 1 to 9,999.
Road Transport Department (JPJ) director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said bids can be placed through the JPJeBid app, with the results to be announced on Sept 21.
He said the H series is special as the last single-letter series JPJ will offer, while also symbolising harmony in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations.
“This series is very special, and the public is encouraged to take this opportunity to bid for a number, as JPJ will not be offering any more single-letter series,” he said at a press conference after the launch of the series here yesterday.
Aedy Fadly said the H series differed from taxi registrations, where the letter H must be accompanied by a state registration letter.
“For example, taxis in Perak are registered with the letters ‘HA’, with ‘A’ representing the state registration letter,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Azalina pushes questions on Najib’s pardon bid to Hannah Yeoh, says BHEUU is just the messenger
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Questions surrounding the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's royal pardon petition should be directed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, says Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The minister for law and institutional reform said that she does not sit as the executive representative on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, noting that the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) under her purview functions strictly as the board's administrative secretariat, NST reported.
"BHEUU is under me, but for the Pardons Board in each state, BHEUU is the secretariat, while the minister and menteri besar of the respective state are the executive representatives on the board.
"Any questions about what happened, why it was deferred and the new date should be directed to the minister responsible, Hannah Yeoh. I have no information at all, so I cannot answer," she told reporters after attending the Program Kayuhan Fashionista: Bulan Kebangsaan Dua Sambutan Satu Jiwa at the Putrajaya Lake Promenade.
Azalina was responding to mounting demands from opposition leaders for the government to clarify why the board postponed deliberations on Najib's application.
Her remarks follow statements by PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who urged the government to issue an immediate explanation, contending that the decision was a matter of significant public interest and would not have occurred automatically.
BHEUU had earlier confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board agreed to defer consideration of Najib's petition to a future sitting.
The decision was made during a meeting chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, at Istana Negara, which also saw royal pardons granted to 65 other prison inmates.
Najib, who has been serving his prison sentence since August 2022 following his conviction in the RM42 million SRC International corruption case, previously had his 12-year jail term halved to six years and his fine reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million during an earlier review by the board in 2024.
The former PM is also serving a separate custodial sentence following his conviction in the 1MDB trial, which is currently under appeal.

Title: Haniff Khatri and family escape unhurt as pre-dawn blaze damages three homes in Gombak (VIDEO)
Article:
GOMBAK, Sept 15 — Three double-storey linked houses, including the home of prominent lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla in Bandar Country Homes here, were damaged in a pre-dawn fire on Tuesday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency distress call regarding the blaze at 3.06am, Sinar Harian reported.
“A total of 15 firefighters and officers from the Rawang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP), assisted by the Batu Arang Fire and Rescue Station, together with fire engines, were deployed to the scene, which is located about eight kilometres away,” he said today.
Upon arriving at 3.17am, fire crews discovered that the blaze had engulfed the upper levels of the three adjoining properties.
“The estimated damage caused by the fire was 80 per cent to the first house, 20 per cent to the second house, and five per cent to the third house,” he said.
The fire also destroyed about 90 per cent of a Perodua Axia parked nearby.
“No casualties were reported in the incident. The fire was brought under control at 4.08am before operations were fully concluded at 6.35am,” he said.
https://www.facebook.com/haniff.khatri/videos/1065345816517923/
Recounting the incident, Mohamed Haniff said the fire is believed to have originated in the first-floor living area, although the exact cause remains under investigation.
“My wife, our two children and I were at home when the incident occurred. I was downstairs watching television and slept downstairs that night, while my two children were upstairs.
“My daughter came out of her room to get a drink of water when she noticed the fire and screamed for me,” he said.
Haniff said that upon hearing her shouts, he rushed upstairs and attempted to combat the flames with buckets of water, but was quickly overwhelmed by the thick smoke.
“The heat and smoke had already entered my chest, so I immediately woke my son and told him to get out of the house before calling the fire department,” he said.
The lawyer credited the prompt arrival and professionalism of the firefighters for preventing serious injury to his family.
“I was truly moved by the firefighters’ efforts. They were excellent and highly efficient.
“Thank God, all four of us are physically safe, but the upper floor of the house is completely gone. Everything up there has been destroyed,” he said.

Title: Four boys drown after falling into deep drain while trying to retrieve football in Kulim
Article:
KULIM, Sept 15 — Four boys died after allegedly falling into a drain while attempting to retrieve a football at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, yesterday evening.
Kulim police Chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said two of the victims died at the scene, while the other two succumbed to their injuries while being taken to Kulim Hospital.
He identified the victims as Muhammad Zafril Arsyad Muhamad Azrin, 12; Muhammad Iman Nuruddin Khairol Anuar, 10; and step-siblings Muhamad Aeril Aziz Muhamad Zafis, 12, and Muhammad Arif Naufan Abdullah, eight.
“Police received a call from a member of the public at 7.45 pm yesterday reporting that four victims had drowned in a retention pond at Taman Desa Kayangan.
“Ambulance personnel confirmed that two victims died at the scene, while the other two passed away while being transported to Kulim Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
Syamsul said all four victims lived near Taman Desa Kayangan.
He said interviews with the victims’ mothers revealed that the boys had left home to play football before the ball reportedly fell into a drain at the location.
“The victims are believed to have attempted to retrieve the ball before falling into the drain,” he said.
He added that there were no witnesses to the incident, while the drain was estimated to be about 10 feet deep and six feet wide.
The bodies were taken to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) in Alor Setar last night for post-mortem examinations. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says Malaysia Day preparations in Kuching on track, internet access for media assured
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 15 — Final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebrations at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) are at a satisfactory level, including the provision of internet facilities for media practitioners.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said an inspection with senior ministry officers tonight found that preparations for the celebration tomorrow were progressing well.
“Attention is given to, among others, the provision of items to be distributed to visitors on the night of the celebration, in addition to ministry-related items that will given out at several locations, including the (Kuching) Waterfront area,” he told reporters after inspecting the final minute preparations and full dress rehearsal for the Malaysia Day Celebrations at the BCKK last night.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.
Fahmi also said internet coverage at BCKK was at an optimum level to ensure media practitioners could carry out their duties throughout the celebrations.
“I have spoken to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to ensure our media friends have sufficient access to the internet, whether via Wi-Fi or mobile networks, to carry out their duties,” he said.
He said the MCMC had informed him that all equipment and hardware, which telecommunications companies needed to install, had been completed and were functioning well.
He added that the next inspection would focus on technical aspects, including the audio system, to ensure the event runs smoothly.
“Yesterday, Communications Ministry secretary-general (Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah) informed us about issues involving the audio system, so we will examine this more closely to ensure that we have a good show ahead of Sept 16,” he said.
About 5,000 people are expected to gather at BCKK on Wednesday for the Malaysia Day Celebrations, which will be graced by the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, and his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi.
The official event, which will begin at 8.15 pm, will also be attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. — Bernama

Title: Unity minister condemns Umno assembly joke on Catholic clergy, urges authorities to act
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang has denounced a controversial remark made during the Umno General Assembly 2026 that used Catholic priests and nuns as the subject of a joke, warning that such conduct crosses a line that must not be tolerated in Malaysia's multi-religious society.
In a media statement today, Dagang said he views the controversy seriously, stressing that jokes touching on religious institutions, religious figures, holy texts or the beliefs of any community are never acceptable, regardless of the intent behind them.
"Religion is not a joke," the minister said, adding that matters held sacred by a community should never be mocked, turned into sexually-toned humour, or exploited merely to draw laughter and applause from a crowd.
Dagang argued that freedom of speech and political expression do not give anyone licence to trample on the religious sensitivities of others, and said this principle must be applied evenly regardless of religion, race, status or political affiliation.
The minister has called on relevant ministries and enforcement agencies to look into the matter and launch investigations if any legal provisions were breached, citing Sections 298 and 298A of the Penal Code as well as related provisions under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
While acknowledging that the individual behind the remark has expressed willingness to apologise, Dagang said he hopes the episode will serve as a reminder to leaders, public speakers and society at large to exercise greater care when addressing matters of religion and belief.
He also linked the controversy to the fifth principle of the Rukun Negara — Courtesy and Morality — describing it as a foundational value that safeguards mutual respect and harmony in Malaysia's diverse society, rather than a mere slogan.

Title: Anwar defends moderate approach on Umno ties, says govt stability must come first
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views regarding the issue of cooperation with Umno within the Unity Government.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman, stated that the government must remain stable because any overly harsh actions concerning the issue could result in losses for the country.
“I choose a somewhat moderate path because what is important is that the government must be stable, otherwise there will be many losses for our country.
“So for me, that is what is important, and I see that, for example, is also the voice we hear including from Umno,” he said during a press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut here, before concluding his working visit to India yesterday.
Elaborating further, Anwar said various views were also voiced among political parties including PH, but such matters are normal within a coalition and should not be seen as something that could threaten government cooperation.
“We listen to everything, but to my knowledge, I don’t see any problems. There are small and normal ones. Even in a household, there are minor issues, let alone with political commanders,” he said.
The Prime Minister said this when asked to comment on his views regarding several issues raised at the 2026 Umno General Assembly (PAU) recently. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Miti to pursue wider market access for Malaysian goods in India
Article:
KERALAM, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) will follow up on efforts to widen access for Malaysian goods to the Indian market, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the matter was discussed during his meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, with several restrictions still needing to be addressed to facilitate trade between the two countries.
“We believe that some restrictions are still in place, for example airlines. We are still requesting for additional facility in some other cities,” said Anwar during a press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut here, before concluding his working visit to India yesterday.
He said the matter was also raised during his meeting with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Malaysia would use the appropriate channels to address the matter and further strengthen trade and investment ties with India.
“This is a concern for the request from the Keralam chief minister. I think that is reasonable, but we need to address it through the right mechanism,” said Anwar.
The Prime Minister emphasised Malaysia’s view of India as a vital economic partner, aiming to strengthen trade and investment between the two nations.
He said widening market access was important to ensure more Malaysian goods could penetrate the Indian market, thereby benefiting local industries and businesses.
Earlier, Anwar and Satheesan discussed efforts to strengthen economic cooperation and facilitate greater trade and investment between Malaysia and India’s southern state, Keralam, formerly known as Kerala.
The discussion took place during Satheesan’s courtesy call on Anwar in Calicut, held in conjunction with the Prime Minister’s working visit to India and his maiden visit to Keralam as Prime Minister.
Anwar arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the BRICS Leaders’ Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and delivered the National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth. — Bernama
